promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: You have the fitness for more, but 53 miles was 15 over the plan and a big jump on the week before, so this week steps back to about 40 miles.

flags.title: Ran over the plan
flags.detail: You ran 53 mi against 38 planned. That included a run on the Monday rest day, a fourth threshold rep and 20 mi instead of 15 on Sunday. This week each session has a hard cap, so stop at the number.

flags.title: Long run effort

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
Not at 53 miles a week, not this soon. Feeling fine is normal after a jump like this, because your heart and lungs adapt faster than your calves, tendons and joints. The cost usually shows up a week or two later.

Your weekly miles show how steep the climb has been:

| Week | Miles |
| --- | --- |
| Aug 24 – 30 | 27 |
| Aug 31 – Sep 6 | 37 |
| Sep 7 – 13 | 53 |
| Sep 14 – 20 (planned) | 40 |

The planned 40 is still above two weeks ago, so you keep building. From here, add about 10% a week, which points to roughly 44 miles next. Your calves were tight on Sunday night, and your right knee hurt on a long run four weeks ago. Those are good reasons to climb in steps rather than jumps.

If you feel great, spend that energy on the quality work in the plan, not on extra miles. Added reps and bonus miles are where this week got away from the plan.

new.analysis:
The fitness behind last week is real. Your easy pace has held at about 9:50 per mile at heart rate 139 for four weeks. Your 20-miler had flat splits and only 7 beats of drift. That tells me your aerobic engine is ahead of the plan, so the limit is how fast your legs absorb the load.

A step back to about 40 miles is a consolidation week, not a punishment. Weekly miles and the long run both rose by roughly 40% in one week. A lighter week now lets your body bank that work, and it means you start the next block fresh instead of finding out in three weeks that something has had enough.

Distance is no longer what you are short of. You have run 20 miles, and the race asks for 8:35 per mile, about 85 seconds faster than your long-run pace. The next long runs should add marathon-pace miles instead of more easy distance. If your calves are fine, the first of those comes next week, a second follows about two weeks later, and then the taper starts.

Easy days protect the hard days. Your short runs sit right where they should, around 139. The long run is where easy slipped, and a moderate effort for over three hours costs more recovery than it feels like at the time.

Wednesday is three reps on purpose. Four reps at 7:55 felt strong, but each extra rep pushes a threshold session toward race effort, and that makes it harder to run the weekend well. Hold 8:00, stop at three, and finish the day feeling you could have done more.

safetyCallouts.title: Calf tightness after the 20-miler.
safetyCallouts.body: Your calves were tight on Sunday night. If they are still tight on Tuesday, shorten that run to 4 mi and skip the Wednesday reps. If the tightness becomes pain that gets worse as you run, stop and see a physio or doctor.
